nodes.name: Dirichlet problem for the elliptic Monge-Amp\`ere equation
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \det (D^2 u) = f \text{ in } \Omega, \quad u=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Solve $\det(D^2u)=f$ in $\Omega$ with the Dirichlet condition $u=g$ on $\partial\Omega$.

nodes.name: Standing assumptions on the domain, the data and the solution
nodes.statement: The domain $\Omega$ is assumed to be a convex polygonal domain of $\R^2$ and \eqref{MA} is assumed to have a strictly convex smooth solution $u \in C^3(\tir{\Omega})$. The function $f \in C^1(\tir{\Omega})$ is given and satisfies $f \geq c_0$ for a constant $c_0 >0$ and the function $g\in C(\partial \Omega)$ is also given and assumed to extend to a $C^3(\tir{\Omega})$ function $G$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega$ convex polygonal, $u\in C^3$ strictly convex, $f\in C^1$ with $f\ge c_0>0$, and $g$ extends to $G\in C^3(\bar\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Notation: Hessian $D^2u$, gradient $Dv$, cofactor matrix $\cof D^2 v$ and the space $V_h$
nodes.statement: In \eqref{MA}, $D^2 u=\big( \partial^2 u/(\partial x_i \partial x_j)\big)_{i,j=1,\ldots, 2} $ is the Hessian matrix of $u$ and $\det$ denotes the determinant operator. Let $V_h$ denote the Lagrange finite element space of degree $k \geq 2$ and let $D v$ denote the gradient of the function $v$. Recall that $\cof D^2 v$ denotes the matrix of cofactors of $D^2 v$.
nodes.statement_short: Fixes the Hessian, the determinant, the degree-$k$ Lagrange space $V_h$, the gradient $Dv$ and the cofactor matrix $\cof D^2v$.

nodes.name: $C^0$ interior penalty discretization in abstract form
nodes.statement: The $C^0$ interior penalty discretization can be written in abstract form as: find $u_h \in V_h$ such that $u_h=g_h$ on $\partial \Omega$ and \begin{align} A(u_h,\phi) & = 0, \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{align} Here $g_h$ denotes the canonical interpolant in $V_h$ of a continuous extension of $g$ and $A$ is defined in \eqref{IP-form} below.
nodes.statement_short: Discrete nonlinear problem: find $u_h\in V_h$ with $u_h=g_h$ on $\partial\Omega$ and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for all $\phi\in V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Existence of a smooth solution on strictly convex smooth domains
nodes.statement: It is known that when $\Omega$ is strictly convex with a smooth boundary, and with our smoothness assumptions on $f$ and $g$, \eqref{MA} has a smooth solution.
nodes.statement_short: On a strictly convex smooth domain the Monge-Amp\`ere Dirichlet problem has a smooth solution.
nodes.origin_citation: classical smooth-solution theory for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation (invoked as known; the paper gives no explicit reference here)
assumptions: when $\Omega$ is strictly convex with a smooth boundary
with our smoothness assumptions on $f$ and $g$

nodes.name: Contribution of the paper and comparison with previous $W^{1,\infty}$ estimates
nodes.statement: There has been no previous study of multilevel methods for finite element discretizations of \eqref{MA}. In addition, we give quasi-optimal $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the discretization with cubic and higher order elements. Localized $W^{1,\infty}$ estimates were obtained in \cite{Neilan2013b} for quadratic and higher order elements on a smooth domain for which an elliptic regularity property holds for a linearization of the continuous problem. It is reasonable to assume that such a regularity property also holds for cubes. With the quasi-optimal $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates we obtain a new proof of the optimal $H^1$ estimates obtained in \cite{Brenner2010b}.
nodes.statement_short: First multilevel study for FE discretizations of Monge-Amp\`ere; quasi-optimal $W^{1,\infty}$ estimates that also re-prove the known optimal $H^1$ estimates.

nodes.name: Triangulation $\mathcal{T}_h$ and its edge sets
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_h$ denote a conforming, shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation of $\Omega$ into simplices $K$. We denote by $\mathcal{E}_h$ the set of edges of $\mathcal{T}_h$, by $\mathcal{E}^b_h$ the set of boundary edges and by $\mathcal{E}^i_h$ the set of interior edges.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{T}_h$ is a conforming, shape regular, quasi-uniform simplicial mesh; $\mathcal{E}_h$, $\mathcal{E}^b_h$, $\mathcal{E}^i_h$ are all, boundary and interior edges.

nodes.name: Mesh size $h$, shape regularity constants and the generic constant $C$
nodes.statement: Let $h_K$ denote the diameter of the element $K$ and put $h=\max_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} h_K$. We assume that $0< h \leq 1$. We recall that, for a shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation, there exists a constant $\sigma >0$ such that $h_K/\rho_K \leq \sigma$, for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ where $\rho_K$ denotes the radius of the largest ball inside $K$ and there is another constant $C$ such that $h \leq C h_K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$. Throughout the paper, we will use the letter $C$ for a generic constant, independent of $h$, which may change from occurrences.
nodes.statement_short: $h=\max_K h_K\le 1$; shape regularity gives $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ and $h\le Ch_K$, and $C$ denotes a generic $h$-independent constant.

nodes.name: Sobolev spaces $W^{s,p}(\Omega)$, $H^s(\Omega)$, $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and their norms
nodes.statement: We use the usual notation $W^{s,p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq s, p \leq \infty$ for the Sobolev spaces of functions in $L^{p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq p \leq \infty$, with weak derivatives up to order $s$ in $L^{p}(\Omega)$. The standard notation $H^s(\Omega)$ is used for $W^{s,2}(\Omega)$ and $H^{1}_{0}(\Omega)$ denotes the subspace of elements in $H^1(\Omega)$ with vanishing trace on the boundary $\partial \Omega$. Similarly, we define $W^{1,\infty}_{0}(\Omega)$. The norm of $v \in W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is denoted $\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ and its seminorm $|v|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$. We will omit the argument $\Omega$ when it is understood from context.
nodes.statement_short: Standard Sobolev space and (semi)norm notation, including $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$.
differentia: with weak derivatives up to order $s$ in $L^{p}(\Omega)$

nodes.name: Polynomial space $P_k(K)$ and the broken Sobolev norms
nodes.statement: Denote by $P_k(K)$ the space of polynomials of degree $k$ on the element $K$. We will need the broken Sobolev norm defined for $1 \leq p < \infty$ by \begin{equation*} \|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\T_h)}=\left(\sum_{K \in \T_h}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(K)}^p\right)^{1/p}, \end{equation*} and for $p=\infty$ by \begin{equation*} \|v\|_{W^{k,\infty}(\T_h)}=\max_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\|v\|_{W^{k,\infty}(K)}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Element-wise broken $W^{k,p}$ norms over $\mathcal{T}_h$, with the $\ell^p$ aggregation for $p<\infty$ and the max for $p=\infty$.

nodes.name: Inverse estimates on $V_h$
nodes.statement: We recall the inverse estimates \cite[Lemma 4.5.3]{Brenner08} \begin{equation} \|v\|_{W^{s,p}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\leq Ch^{t-s+\min(0,\frac{2}{p}-\frac{2}{q})}\|v\|_{W^{t,q}(\mathcal{T}_h)}, \forall v\in V_h, \end{equation} valid for $0\leq t \leq s$ and $1\leq p,q \leq \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Broken-norm inverse inequality trading derivatives for negative powers of $h$ on the finite element space.
assumptions: valid for $0\leq t \leq s$ and $1\leq p,q \leq \infty$

nodes.name: Trace inequality and its scaled element form
nodes.statement: We also recall the trace inequality \cite[Theorem 1.6.6]{Brenner08}, $\|v\|_{L^p(\partial \Omega)}\leq C \|v\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}, 1 \leq p \leq \infty$ which gives by a scaling argument \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^p(\partial K)}\leq C h^{-\frac{1}{p}} (||v||_{L^p(K)} + h ||D v||_{L^p(K)} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $L^p$ trace inequality, rescaled to give $\|v\|_{L^p(\partial K)}\le Ch^{-1/p}(\|v\|_{L^p(K)}+h\|Dv\|_{L^p(K)})$.

nodes.name: Edgewise $L^1$ bound for $W^{1,1}$ functions
nodes.statement: For $\phi \in W^{1,1}(\Omega)$, by the trace estimate \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{align} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i} \|\phi\|_{L^1(e)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}(K)} =C h^{-1} \|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Summing the trace estimate over interior edges gives $\sum_e\|\phi\|_{L^1(e)}\le Ch^{-1}\|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}}$.

nodes.name: Scaled trace inverse inequality on $V_h$
nodes.statement: By an inverse estimate one has from \eqref{trace-estimate} \begin{equation} ||v||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} ||v||_{L^2(K)} \, \forall v \in V_h. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\|v\|_{L^2(\partial K)}\le Ch^{-1/2}\|v\|_{L^2(K)}$ for discrete functions.

nodes.name: Approximation properties of the Lagrange interpolant $I_h$
nodes.statement: We will also need the following properties of the Lagrange interpolant operator $I_h$ \cite[Corollary 4.4.24]{Brenner08} \begin{align} ||v-I_h v||_{W^{s,p}(\mathcal{T}_h)} & \leq C h^{k+1-s} ||v||_{W^{k+1,p}}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty, v \in W^{k+1,p}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Local interpolation error estimate
nodes.statement: This follows from our assumptions on the triangulation and \cite[ (4.4.5) ]{Brenner08}, i.e. for $ v \in W^{k+1,p}(K)$ \begin{equation} |v-I_h v|_{W^{s,p}(K)} \leq C h^{k+1-s}_K |v|_{W^{k+1,p}(K)}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Elementwise seminorm bound $|v-I_hv|_{W^{s,p}(K)}\le Ch_K^{k+1-s}|v|_{W^{k+1,p}(K)}$.

nodes.name: Boundary gradient estimate for the interpolation error
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{trace-estimate} and \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} that \begin{equation} \begin{split} || D( I_h u - u) ||_{L^{2}(\partial K)} & \leq C h^{- \frac{1}{2} } || D( I_h u - u) ||_{L^{2}(K)} + C h^{ \frac{1}{2} } || D(I_h u - u) ||_{H^{1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{k- \frac{1}{2}} || u ||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Frobenius inner product $A:B$ and divergence of a matrix field
nodes.statement: For two matrices $A$ and $B$, $A:B = \sum^2_{i,j=1}A_{ij}B_{ij}$ denotes their Frobenius inner product. The divergence of a matrix field is understood as the vector obtained by taking the divergence of each row.

nodes.name: Determinant as half the Frobenius product of the Hessian with its cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: The following results can be checked by simple algebraic computations and can also be found in \cite{AwanouLiMixed1}. For $v$ sufficiently smooth we have \begin{equation} \det D^2 v = \frac{1}{2} (\cof D^2 v): D^2 v, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\det D^2v=\tfrac12(\cof D^2v):D^2v$ for smooth $v$ in two dimensions.
conclusions: \det D^2 v = \frac{1}{2} (\cof D^2 v): D^2 v

nodes.name: Fr\'echet derivative of $F(v)=\det D^2 v - f$
nodes.statement: and if $F(v) = \det D^2 v -f$, the Fr\'echet derivative of $F$ at $v$ is given by \begin{equation} F'(v) w = (\cof D^2 v): D^2 w, \end{equation} for $v,w$ sufficiently smooth.
nodes.statement_short: The linearization of the Monge-Amp\`ere operator is $F'(v)w=(\cof D^2v):D^2w$.
conclusions: F'(v) w = (\cof D^2 v): D^2 w

nodes.name: Row divergence-free property of the cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: Under the same assumptions \begin{equation} \div\big((\cof D^2 w) D v )= (\cof D^2 w): D^2 v, \end{equation} which is a consequence of the product rule and the row divergence-free property of the Hessian, i.e. $\div( \cof D^2 w) =0$.
nodes.statement_short: Because $\div(\cof D^2w)=0$, the product rule gives $\div((\cof D^2w)Dv)=(\cof D^2w):D^2v$.
conclusions: \div\big((\cof D^2 w) D v )= (\cof D^2 w): D^2 v

nodes.name: Divergence form of the linearized Monge-Amp\`ere operator
nodes.statement: It then follows that \begin{equation} F'(u)v= \div \big((\cof D^2 u) D v \big). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $F'(u)v=\div((\cof D^2u)Dv)$, i.e. the linearization is a divergence-form elliptic operator.

nodes.name: Additivity of the cofactor operator in two dimensions
nodes.statement: Note that \begin{equation} \cof(D^2 v +D^2 w) = \cof(D^2 v) + \cof(D^2 w), \end{equation} since we restrict our discussion to the two dimensional case.
nodes.statement_short: In 2D the cofactor map is linear: $\cof(D^2v+D^2w)=\cof(D^2v)+\cof(D^2w)$.
assumptions: since we restrict our discussion to the two dimensional case

nodes.name: Difference of determinants formula
nodes.statement: We have \cite{Brenner2010b} \begin{equation} \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2} (\cof(D^2 v) + \cof(D^2 w)): (D^2 v - D^2 w). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\det D^2v-\det D^2w=\tfrac12(\cof(D^2v)+\cof(D^2w)):(D^2v-D^2w)$.
conclusions: \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2} (\cof(D^2 v) + \cof(D^2 w)): (D^2 v - D^2 w)

nodes.name: Divergence form of the difference of determinants
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{det2}, \eqref{linearity} and \eqref{det5}, we obtain \begin{equation} \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2}\div \Big( \big( \cof D^2 (v+w)\big) D(v -w)\Big). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\det D^2v-\det D^2w=\tfrac12\div((\cof D^2(v+w))D(v-w))$.
conclusions: \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2}\div \Big( \big( \cof D^2 (v+w)\big) D(v -w)\Big)

nodes.name: Uniform positive definiteness of $\cof D^2 u$
nodes.statement: We recall that $u$ is strictly convex and thus $\cof D^2 u $ is uniformly positive definite; that is, there exists positive constants $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ such that $\forall x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ \begin{equation} \alpha_0 |r|^2 \leq r^T (\cof D^2 u(x) ) r \leq \alpha_1 |r|^2, \quad \forall r \in \mathbb{R}^2. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Strict convexity of $u$ makes $\cof D^2u$ uniformly elliptic: $\alpha_0|r|^2\le r^T(\cof D^2u)r\le\alpha_1|r|^2$.

nodes.name: Discrete (elementwise) Hessian $D^2 v$ for $v \in V_h$
nodes.statement: For $v \in V_h$, we will make the abuse of notation of denoting by $D^2v$ the discrete Hessian of $v$ computed element by element.

nodes.name: Jump of a vector field across an interior edge
nodes.statement: For $e \subset \partial K$, let $n_K$ denote the outward normal to $K$ and let $v|_K$ denote the restriction of the field $v$ to $K$. For $e=K^+ \cap K^-$, we define the jump of the vector field $v$ across $e$ as \begin{equation} \[v\]_e=v|_{K^+} \cdot n_{K^+} + v|_{K^-} \cdot n_{K^-}, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $[\![v]\!]_e = v|_{K^+}\cdot n_{K^+}+v|_{K^-}\cdot n_{K^-}$, the normal jump across $e=K^+\cap K^-$.
nodes.definiendum: the jump of the vector field $v$ across $e$

nodes.name: Average of a vector field on an interior edge
nodes.statement: and its average on $e$ as \begin{equation} \{\!\{v\}\!\}_e= \frac{1}{2}(v|_{K^+} + v|_{K^-} ). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Jump and average of a matrix field on an interior edge
nodes.statement: The jump and average of a matrix field $E$ on $e$ are defined respectively as \begin{equation} \[E\]_e=n_{K^+}^T E|_{K^+} +n_{K^-}^T E|_{K^-}, \end{equation}
nodes.definiendum: The jump and average of a matrix field $E$ on $e$

nodes.name: Jump-average product rule for a matrix field times a vector field
nodes.statement: For a matrix field $E$ and a vector field $v$ it is not difficult to check that for $e \in \mathcal{E}^i_h$ \begin{equation} \[Ev\]_e=\[\{\!\{E\}\!\}_e v\]_e+\[E\]_e\{\!\{v\}\!\}_e. \end{equation}
assumptions: For a matrix field $E$ and a vector field $v$

nodes.name: Elliptic projection $P_h u$ associated with $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{P}_h:H_0^1(\Omega) \rightarrow V_h$ denote the projection with respect to the bilinear form $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$ and recall that $G$ denotes a $C^3(\tir{\Omega})$ extension of $g$. We define $$ P_h u = \hat{P}_h(u-G) + I_h G, $$ where $I_h$ denotes the canonical Lagrange interpolant operator into $V_h$.
nodes.statement_short: $P_hu=\hat P_h(u-G)+I_hG$, the $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$-projection corrected by the interpolant of the boundary extension.

nodes.name: Defining relation for the projection error of $P_h u$
nodes.statement: Then $P_h u = I_h u$ on $\partial \Omega$ and \begin{equation} A'(u;P_h u - u, \phi) = A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) ,~ \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $A'(u;P_hu-u,\phi)=A'(u;I_hG-G,\phi)$ for all discrete test functions.

nodes.name: $W^{1,\infty}$ projection error bound and the constant $C_1$
nodes.statement: It thus follows from the approximation properties of $I_h$ that \begin{equation} ||u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} \equiv C_1 h^k, \ \text{for } u \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\|u-P_hu\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\le Ch^k\|u\|_{W^{k+1,\infty}}\equiv C_1h^k$.

nodes.name: Broken $W^{2,\infty}$ projection error bound
nodes.statement: By an inverse estimate, \eqref{2grid-proj1}, and the approximation properties of $I_h$, we have \begin{align*} ||u-P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} &\leq ||u-I_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} + ||I_h u -P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \\ & \leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} + C h^{-1} \big( ||I_h u - u||_{W^{1,\infty}} + || u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \big), \end{align*} that is \begin{align} ||u-P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} &\leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\|u-P_hu\|_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\le Ch^{k-1}\|u\|_{W^{k+1,\infty}}$.

nodes.name: Discrete Green's functions $g^z_{h,i}$ and $G^z_h$
nodes.statement: Following \cite{Xu1996}, we will obtain pointwise estimates via the use of discrete Green's functions. For $z\in \Omega \setminus \cup_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\partial K$, let $g^z_{h,i} \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega)$, $i=1,2$ be defined by: \begin{equation} A'(u; g^z_{h,i},\phi)=\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x_i}(z), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega), \end{equation} and let $G^z_h$ be defined by \begin{equation} A'(u;G^z_h,\phi) = \phi (z), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $g^z_{h,i}$ and $G^z_h$ are the discrete Green's functions for $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$ representing $\partial_i\phi(z)$ and $\phi(z)$.

nodes.name: Logarithmic $W^{1,1}$ bounds for the discrete Green's functions
nodes.statement: We have for $h$ sufficiently small \begin{equation} \|g^z_{h,i}\|_{W^{1,1}} \leq C |\ln h|, \end{equation} and \begin{align*} \|G^z_h\|_{L^{2}} \leq C, \end{align*} where the constant $C$ is independent of $z$. In the case $\cof D^2 u$ is the identity matrix, the proof is given in \cite[Lemmas 2.1 and 3.3]{ThomeeXuZhang}. The proof of the general case is similar \cite{Malitz-thesis}. Moreover we have \cite{Malitz-thesis}, see also \cite[Exercise 8.x.19]{Brenner08}, \begin{align} \|G^z_h\|_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Both discrete Green's functions obey $\|\cdot\|_{W^{1,1}}\le C|\ln h|$, with $C$ independent of $z$.
nodes.origin_citation: Thom\'ee, Xu & Zhang 1989, Lemmas 2.1 and 3.3; Malitz 2018

nodes.name: Proof of the $W^{1,1}$ bound for $G^z_h$
nodes.statement: It is enough to prove that $|G^z_h |_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|$ which follows from the bound $| G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} $ and H\"older's inequality. By the discrete Sobolev inequality \cite[(4.9.2)]{Brenner08} and the coercivity of the form $A'(u; .,.)$, we have for $h$ sufficiently small \begin{align*} | A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h) | = | G^z_h (z)| \leq || G^z_h ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} || G^z_h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*} It follows that $$ | G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}}, $$ giving the claimed bound.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $|G^z_h|_{W^{1,2}}\le C|\ln h|^{1/2}$ via H\"older, then use the discrete Sobolev inequality and coercivity of $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$.

nodes.name: $C^0$ interior penalty bilinear-form operator $A(v,\phi)$
nodes.statement: We first describe the interior penalty discretization proposed in \cite{Brenner2010b} for polygonal domains and with the boundary condition enforced strongly. For $\phi \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ and $v \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$, we define \begin{equation} A(v,\phi) := \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (f-\det D^2 v) \phi \ud x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi \ud s. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $A(v,\phi)$ combines the elementwise residual $\int_K(f-\det D^2v)\phi$ with interior-edge penalty terms built from $\{\!\{\cof D^2v\}\!\}Dv$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Fr\'echet derivative of $A$ evaluated at the exact solution $u$
nodes.statement: The addition of the penalty terms, the second term on the right of \eqref{IP-form}, to the natural discretization of \eqref{MA} is motivated by the need in the analysis that the Fr\'echet derivative evaluated at $u$ of the mapping $v \to A(v,\phi)$ is given by \begin{equation} A'(u;v,\phi)= \int_{\Omega} \big( (\cof D^2 u) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x. \end{equation} This is proven in \cite[p. 5]{Brenner2010b}.
nodes.statement_short: At $u$ the linearization collapses to the standard elliptic form $A'(u;v,\phi)=\int_\Omega((\cof D^2u)Dv)\cdot D\phi$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Taylor remainder $R(w;v,\phi)$ of $w \mapsto A(w,\phi)$
nodes.statement: Let $R(w;v,\phi)$ denote the remainder of the Taylor expansion at $w$ of $w \mapsto A(w,\phi)$, i.e. \begin{equation} A(w+v,\phi)=A(w,\phi)+A'(w;v,\phi) + R(w;v,\phi). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
nodes.definiendum: the remainder of the Taylor expansion at $w$ of $w \mapsto A(w,\phi)$

nodes.name: Fr\'echet derivative and remainder of the interior penalty form
nodes.statement: For $v, w \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ and $\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega)$, we have \begin{align} \begin{split} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K }\big( (\cof D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x \\ & \quad - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 w)\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\} \phi \ud s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s, \end{split} \end{align} and \begin{align} R(w;v,\phi) = -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\det D^2v)\phi\ud x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s. \end{align} In particular, for $u \in C^3(\Omega)$, \eqref{Frechet-at-u} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for $A'(w;v,\phi)$ and $R(w;v,\phi)$; at $w=u\in C^3$ the edge terms vanish and $A'$ reduces to the elliptic form.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
assumptions: For $v, w \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ and $\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega)$
conclusions: A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K }\big( (\cof D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x
R(w;v,\phi) = -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\det D^2v)\phi\ud x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s

nodes.name: Proof of the Fr\'echet derivative formula
nodes.statement: For $w,v \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ we have \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big(\det D^2(w+v)-\det D^2w\big)\phi\ud x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 (w+v) \}\!\} D (w+v) \] \phi \ud s - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s, \end{multline*} for all $\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Since $D^2 w$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix, $\det D^2(w+v)= \det D^2 w + \det D^2 v +\cof D^2 w : D^2 v$. Thus \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\det D^2v)\phi\ud x -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\cof D^2 w: D^2v)\phi\ud x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi\ud s. + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s. \end{multline*} By \eqref{det2} $\cof D^2 w: D^2 v = \div\big((\cof D^2 w) D v )$. This implies that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \div \big((\cof D^2 w) D v\big) \phi \ud x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \ud s \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s, \end{align*} and $R(w;v,\phi)$ is given by \eqref{rdef1}. By integration by parts and using the fact $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big((\cof D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 w) D v \] \phi \ud x \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \ud s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s . \end{align*} By \eqref{jumpaverage}, $ \[(\cof D^2 w) D v\] = \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] + \[\cof D^2 w\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\}. $ It follows that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K }\big( (\cof D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 w)\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\} \phi \ud s \\\notag & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s . \end{align*} Finally, since by assumption $u \in C^3(\Omega)$, $\[(\cof D^2 u)\]=0$. In addition, by definition $\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\}$ is continuous and $Du$ is continuous by the assumption on $u$. Thus $\[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D u \]=0$ on each interior edge. The statement about $A'(u;v,\phi)$ easily follows.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)$, use the 2D determinant expansion and $\div(\cof D^2w)=0$, integrate by parts, then split the jump with the product rule.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Simplified expression for the remainder $R(w;v,\phi)$
nodes.statement: We have for $\phi \in H_0^{1}(\Omega)$ and $v, w \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$, \begin{multline} R(w;v,\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \ud x \\ -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 v) \] \{\!\{ D v \}\!\} \phi \ud s + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[ \{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: $R(w;v,\phi)$ equals a half-weighted sum of an elementwise gradient term and two interior-edge jump/average terms.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
assumptions: for $\phi \in H_0^{1}(\Omega)$ and $v, w \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$
conclusions: R(w;v,\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \ud x

nodes.name: Proof of the simplified remainder formula
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{det1} and integration by parts \begin{multline*} \int_{K} (\det D^2 v ) \phi \ud x = \frac{1}{2} \int_{K} (\cof D^2 v ): (D^2 v) \, \phi \ud x = \frac{1}{2} \int_{K} \div\big((\cof D^2 v) D v ) \phi \ud x \\ =- \frac{1}{2} \int_K [(\cof D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \ud x + \frac{1}{2} \int_{\partial K} \big[ (\cof D^2 v) D v \big] \cdot n_K \phi \ud s. \end{multline*} By definition of jump and since $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{\partial K} \big( (\cof D^2 v) D v \big) \cdot n_K \phi \ud s & = \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 v) D v \] \phi \ud s . \end{align} We conclude that \begin{multline*} R(w;v,\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \ud x -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 v) D v \] \phi \ud s \\ + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s. \end{multline*} Therefore, using \eqref{jumpaverage} to expand the term $\[(\cof D^2 v) D v \] $ we obtain \eqref{R1-simple}.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the determinant identity by parts on each element, convert the boundary sums into edge jumps, then expand with the jump-average product rule.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Nonlinear fixed-point operator $\Phi: V_h \to V_h$
nodes.statement: We define a nonlinear operator $\Phi: V_h \to V_h$ by $ v_h = \Phi( v_h)$ on $\partial \Omega$ and \begin{equation} A'(u; v_h-\Phi( v_h),\phi) = A_{}( v_h,\phi), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi$ is one linearized (Newton-type) correction: $A'(u;v_h-\Phi(v_h),\phi)=A(v_h,\phi)$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Fixed points of $\Phi$ solve the discrete nonlinear problem
nodes.statement: A fixed point of $\Phi$ is a solution of the nonlinear finite element problem \eqref{IP-abstract}.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
conclusions: A fixed point of $\Phi$ is a solution of the nonlinear finite element problem \eqref{IP-abstract}

nodes.name: Bounds defining the constants $C_2$, $C_3$ and $C_4$
nodes.statement: We note that by \eqref{nodal-interpolant}, \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound} and \eqref{green-0} \begin{align*} | A'(u;I_h G - G, G^z_h) | & \leq C_2 h^k | \ln h| \\ | A'(u;I_h G - G, g^z_{h,i}) | & \leq C_3 h^k | \ln h|. \end{align*} We then define $C_4= \max\{ C_1, C_2, C_3 \}$ where the constant $C_1$ is defined in \eqref{2grid-proj1}.
nodes.statement_short: The boundary-extension consistency terms are $O(h^k|\ln h|)$, which fixes $C_4=\max\{C_1,C_2,C_3\}$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: The closed ball $B_h$ of discrete functions near $u$
nodes.statement: Consider the closed set \begin{equation} B_h = \{ v \in V_h: v=g_h \text{ on } \partial \Omega, ||v-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 3 C_4 h^{k} |\ln h |\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $B_h$ is the set of discrete functions matching $g_h$ on the boundary and within $3C_4h^k|\ln h|$ of $u$ in $W^{1,\infty}$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Non-emptiness of $B_h$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{2grid-proj1} $P_h u \in B_h$ and hence $B_h$ is non-empty.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
conclusions: $P_h u \in B_h$ and hence $B_h$ is non-empty

nodes.name: Invariance of $B_h$ under $\Phi$
nodes.statement: We have $\Phi( B_h) \subset B_h$ for $h$ sufficiently small and $k \geq 3$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Proof that $\Phi$ maps $B_h$ into itself
nodes.statement: For $v_h \in B_h$, we have using \eqref{Phi-def} and \eqref{2grid-proj-def} \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) + A'(u; u - P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{split} \end{align*} By definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and since $A(u,\phi)=0$, we have $$ -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = A(u,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$ We conclude that \begin{align} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{align} Therefore, using \eqref{R1-simple}, \eqref{w11-phi} and \eqref{Frechet-at-u}, we have \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} \\ +C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } || \phi ||_{L^1(e)} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) | \\ \leq C h^{-1} || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)|. \end{multline*} By definition of $B_h$, $||v_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h |$. Moreover, by triangle inequality, \eqref{2grid-proj2} and an inverse estimate $||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq ||v_h-P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} + ||P_h u-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h | + C h^{k-1} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h | $. Thus \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C h^{k-2} |\ln h | \, || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} h^{k} |\ln h | + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| \\ \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 ) h^{k} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + | A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| . \end{multline*} Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain using the definition of $C_4$ $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 + C_4 ) h^{k } |\ln h|. $$ Since $C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 \leq C_4$ for $h$ sufficiently small and $k \geq 3$, we get $\|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 2 C_4 h^{k } |\ln h|$. By triangular inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $A'(u;\Phi(v_h)-P_hu,\phi)$ as a residual plus consistency term, bound it by the remainder estimate, then test with the discrete Green's functions.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Algebraic identity for a product of two linear functionals
nodes.statement: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be linear functionals and let $L$ denote their product, i.e. $L(v) = L_1(v) L_2(v)$. We have $$ L(w-u) - L(v-u) = L_1(w-v)L_2(w-u) + L_1(v-u) L_2 (w-v). $$
nodes.statement_short: A telescoping identity splitting $L(w-u)-L(v-u)$ into two products, each carrying a factor $w-v$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
assumptions: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be linear functionals and let $L$ denote their product, i.e. $L(v) = L_1(v) L_2(v)$

nodes.name: Proof of the algebraic product identity
nodes.statement: We have using the linearity of $L_1$ and $L_2$ \begin{align*} L(w-u) - L(v-u) & = L_1(w-u)L_2(w-u) - L_1(v-u) L_2 (v-u) \\ & = [L_1(w-v) + L_1(v-u)] L_2(w-u) - L_1(v-u) L_2 (v-u) \\ & = L_1(w-v)L_2(w-u) + L_1(v-u) [ L_2(w-u) - L_2 (v-u) ], \end{align*} from which the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Add and subtract $L_1(v-u)L_2(w-u)$ and use linearity of $L_1$ and $L_2$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: $\Phi$ is a strict contraction on $B_h$
nodes.statement: The mapping $\Phi$ is a strict contraction in $B_h$ for $h$ sufficiently small and $k \geq 2$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
conclusions: The mapping $\Phi$ is a strict contraction in $B_h$

nodes.name: Proof that $\Phi$ is a strict contraction
nodes.statement: For $v_h$ and $w_h$ in $B_h$, we have \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- w_h,\phi) \\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad + A'(u;w_h - \Phi( w_h),\phi)\\ &= A_{}( w_h,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- w_h,\phi) \\ &= A_{}( w_h,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h -u,\phi) + A'(u; u - w_h,\phi). \end{split} \end{align*} Since $A(u,\phi)=0$, by definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, we have $$ A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) = R(u;w_h-u,\phi) - R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$ Using algebraic manipulations of the type identified in Lemma \ref{algebraic} and \eqref{R1-simple}, we obtain \begin{multline} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 (w_h - v_h) ) D (w_h - u) ] \cdot D \phi \ud x \\ + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 (v_h - u) ) D (w_h - v_h) ] \cdot D \phi \ud x \\ -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \bigg( \[(\cof D^2 (w_h-v_h)) \] \{\!\{ D (w_h-u) \}\!\} + \[(\cof D^2 (v_h-u)) \] \{\!\{ D (w_h-v_h) \}\!\} \bigg) \phi \ud s \\ + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \bigg( \[ \{\!\{\cof D^2 (w_h-v_h) \}\!\} D (w_h-u) \] + \[ \{\!\{\cof D^2 (v_h-u) \}\!\} D (w_h-v_h) \] \bigg) \phi\ud s. \end{multline} Arguing as in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant} and using \eqref{w11-phi}, we obtain \begin{multline*} |A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) | \leq C \Big( || w_h- v_h||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h) } ||w_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \\ + ||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \Big) ||\phi ||_{W^{1,1}}. \end{multline*} As in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant}, we have $||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h|$ and recall that $||w_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h|$ by definition of $B_h$. Moreover, by an inverse estimate $|| w_h- v_h||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h) } \leq C h^{-1} || w_h- v_h||_{W^{1,\infty} }$. We conclude that $$ |A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) | \leq C\big( h^{k-1} |\ln h|+h^{k-1} |\ln h| \big)||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}||\phi ||_{W^{1,1}}. $$ Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h) \|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C ( h^{k-1}+h^{k-1} )|\ln h|^2 ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}, $$ that is, for $k \geq 2$ and $h$ sufficiently small, we have $ \|\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h) \|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 1/2 ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Express $\Phi(v_h)-\Phi(w_h)$ as a difference of remainders, split it with the product identity of Lemma 3.4, and bound it by $Ch^{k-1}|\ln h|^2\|v_h-w_h\|$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Existence, uniqueness and quasi-optimal $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimate
nodes.statement: Problem \eqref{IP-abstract} has a unique solution $u_h$ in $B_h$ for $k \geq 3$, $h$ sufficiently small and $$||u-u_h||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h |.$$
nodes.statement_short: The interior penalty problem has a unique solution in $B_h$ with $\|u-u_h\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\le Ch^k|\ln h|$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization
conclusions: Problem \eqref{IP-abstract} has a unique solution $u_h$ in $B_h$

nodes.name: Improvement of the rate for homogeneous boundary conditions
nodes.statement: We note that in the case of a homogeneous boundary condition, $G=0$ and the right hand side of \eqref{2grid-proj-def} vanishes. In that case, the right hand side of \eqref{expr-inv} simplifies and the rate of convergence in the $W^{1,\infty}$ norm can be shown to be optimal. In other words, Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm} can be improved with suitable estimates of the Ritz projection with a non homogeneous boundary condition.
nodes.statement_short: With $G=0$ the consistency term vanishes and the $W^{1,\infty}$ rate becomes optimal, so Theorem 3.6 could be sharpened.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Optimal $H^1$ error estimate
nodes.statement: Problem \eqref{IP-abstract} has a unique solution $u_h$ in $B_h$ for $k \geq 3$, $h$ sufficiently small and $$||u-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{k}. $$
nodes.statement_short: The same discrete solution satisfies the optimal-order estimate $\|u-u_h\|_{H^1}\le Ch^k$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Proof of the optimal $H^1$ error estimate
nodes.statement: The proof is based on the expression \eqref{expr-con} of $A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi)$ derived in the proof of Lemma \ref{contraction} and the expression \eqref{expr-inv} of $A'(u; \Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi )$ derived in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant}. Since $\Phi(u_h) = u_h$, we have \begin{align} \begin{split} A'(u; u_h - P_h u,\phi) & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - P_h u,\phi) \\ & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi) + A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi). \end{split} \end{align} In view of \eqref{expr-con}, we obtain \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u-u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + \\ C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h- P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \\ + C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)}. \end{multline} By an inverse estimate, Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm}, triangle inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, we have $||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| $. Similarly, using \eqref{2grid-proj2}, we have $||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h|$. Next, by the scaled trace inverse inequality \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}( K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{-1} || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} By \eqref{bramble}, an inverse estimate and \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} \begin{align*} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}\\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{align*} We have $|| P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k ||u||_{H^{k+1}}$. This follows from \cite[Theorem 5.4.4]{Brenner08} in the case of homogeneous boundary conditions. The proof of the general case is similar to \eqref{2grid-proj1}. Thus $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ^2 \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} \leq C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$ As with \eqref{u-p-03}, by \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it follows that \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2} } \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} We conclude from \eqref{u-p-02}--\eqref{u-p-04} that \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline*} Therefore since by Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm} we have the suboptimal estimate $ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^k | \ln h| $ \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}\\ \leq C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$. By \eqref{expr-inv}, we have $$ A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;P_h u-u,\phi) + A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). $$ Using \eqref{R1-simple} and inverse estimates as for \eqref{u-p-04}, we obtain \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} +C\|I_hG-G\|_{H^1}\|\phi\|_{H^1}, \end{multline*} i.e. \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ( h^{k-1} |\ln h| h^k + h^{k-2} |\ln h| h^k + h^k ) ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$. Taking $\phi = u_h - P_h u $ in \eqref{u-p-01} and using \eqref{u-p-05} and \eqref{u-p-06}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality and $k \geq 3$, for $h$ sufficiently small $$ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq Ch^k. $$ This completes the proof by a triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\Phi(u_h)=u_h$ to split $A'(u;u_h-P_hu,\phi)$ into a contraction term and a consistency term, bound each by $Ch^k\|\phi\|_{H^1}$, then take $\phi=u_h-P_hu$.
