nodes.name: The two-grid discretization technique
nodes.statement: The two-grid discretization for solving nonlinear problems is a well established technique. The nonlinear problem \eqref{IP-abstract} is first solved on a coarse mesh of size $H$. The solution $u_H$ is used as an initial guess for one step of Newton's method on the finer mesh of size $h$. Both steps are inexpensive and the method is more efficient than solving the problem through multiple iterations of Newton's method directly on the fine mesh.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the nonlinear problem on a coarse mesh of size $H$, then take one Newton step on the fine mesh of size $h$; both steps are cheap.

nodes.name: Uniform positive definiteness of the discrete Hessian $D^2 u_H$
nodes.statement: Since $u$ is smooth and strictly convex, the smallest eigenvalue of $D^2 u$ is uniformly bounded from below. Thus by the continuity of the eigenvalues of the Hessian as a function of its entries and by approximation, $D^2 u_H$ is uniformly positive definite on each element for $H$ sufficiently small. A detailed argument was given in \cite[Lemma 4]{AwanouPseudo10} in the context of $C^1$ approximations.
nodes.statement_short: For $H$ small the coarse-grid Hessian $D^2u_H$ stays uniformly positive definite elementwise, by eigenvalue continuity and approximation.
assumptions: Since $u$ is smooth and strictly convex
conclusions: $D^2 u_H$ is uniformly positive definite on each element for $H$ sufficiently small

nodes.name: Two-grid algorithm
nodes.statement: {\bf Two-grid algorithm} \begin{enumerate} \item[1.] find $u_H \in V_H$, $u_H=g_H$ on $\partial \Omega$, and $A(u_H,\chi) = 0, ~ \forall ~\chi \in V_H\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, \item[2.] find $u^h \in V_h$, $u^h=g_h$ on $\partial \Omega$, and $A'(u_H;u^h-u_H,\phi)=-A(u_H,\phi), ~\forall ~\phi \in V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Solve the nonlinear interior penalty system on the coarse space $V_H$, then take a single Newton correction in the fine space $V_h$.

nodes.name: Coarse-grid nonlinear solve
nodes.statement: \item[1.] find $u_H \in V_H$, $u_H=g_H$ on $\partial \Omega$, and $A(u_H,\chi) = 0, ~ \forall ~\chi \in V_H\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$,
nodes.statement_short: Solve the full nonlinear interior penalty problem on the coarse space $V_H$.

nodes.name: One Newton step on the fine grid
nodes.statement: \item[2.] find $u^h \in V_h$, $u^h=g_h$ on $\partial \Omega$, and $A'(u_H;u^h-u_H,\phi)=-A(u_H,\phi), ~\forall ~\phi \in V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take one linearized Newton correction about $u_H$ in the fine space $V_h$.

nodes.name: Optimal $H^1$ convergence of the two-grid solution
nodes.statement: We have the estimate \begin{equation} ||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k, \end{equation} for $k \geq 3, H=h^{\lambda}, 1> \lambda> 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k), 0< \epsilon <1$ and $h$ sufficiently small.
nodes.statement_short: For $H=h^\lambda$ with $\lambda>1/2+(2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ the two-grid solution matches the fine-grid solution to $O(h^k)$ in $H^1$.

nodes.name: Proof of the two-grid convergence estimate
nodes.statement: By definition of the two-grid algorithm, the definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for $\phi \in V_h\cap W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$, we have \begin{align*} A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi)&= A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_H-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A(u_H,\phi) \\ & = A(u_h,\phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi) = - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*} It follows that \begin{align*} A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi)& = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*} With arguments similar to the ones used in the proof of Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm}, we have \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline} But, using \eqref{bramble}, \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} and an inverse estimate \begin{align*} | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | u - I_H u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}( K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}( K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} ( K)}. \end{align*} It follows that $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} }. $$ We therefore obtain from \eqref{nodal-interpolant} and Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, \eqref{trace-inverse} and an inverse estimate, it follows that $$ \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{- \frac{3}{2}} H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}}. $$ Therefore, since $|| u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C H^{k-1} |\ln H|$ and by the discrete Sobolev inequality, c.f. \cite{Bramble86}, $|| \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C (1+ | \ln h|^{ 1/2 }) ||\phi||_{H^1}$, we obtain from \eqref{u-p-066} \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} | \ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1} + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \\ \leq C h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline} Using \eqref{R1-simple} and the trace estimates \eqref{trace-inverse} and \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{multline} |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \leq C || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^{-2} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} Taking $\phi = u_h - u^h $ in \eqref{u-p-07} and using \eqref{u-p-08}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality, Theorems \ref{2grid-imp-thm} and \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} for $k \geq 3$ and $h$ sufficiently small \begin{multline*} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C (h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| + H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| ) || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \\ +C h^{-2} (h^{k} |\ln h | + H^{k} |\ln H |) (h^k+H^k). \end{multline*} We conclude that for $H=h^{\lambda}$, $\lambda > \max \{1/(k-1), 3/(2k-1) \} = 3/(2k-1)$ and $k \geq 3$, $$ || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{-2} |\ln H \, | H^{2k}. $$ We therefore get $||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k$ provided $\lambda > 3/(2k-1)$ and $2 \lambda k -2- \epsilon > k$ for some $\epsilon \in (0,1) $, that is $\lambda > \max \{ (k+2+ \epsilon)/(2k), 3/(2k-1) \} = 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $A'(u;u_h-u^h,\phi)$ as a coarse-grid remainder plus a perturbation of the bilinear form, bound each factor by powers of $H$ and $h$, and choose $\lambda$ so the resulting rate is $O(h^k)$.

nodes.name: Smooth convex test problem $u(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ on the unit square
nodes.statement: The computational domain is taken to be the unit square $[0,1]^2$. A uniform grid is obtained by dividing the domain into smaller equal size squares, then dividing each square into two triangles by taking the diagonal with positive slope. We consider a smooth convex test function $u(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ so that $f(x,y)=(1+x^2+y^2)e^{(x^2+y^2)}$ and $g(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ on $\partial \Omega$. While our convergence analysis is only for cubic and higher order elements, we believe the results should be true for quadratic elements. We show numerical convergence of the two-grid solution $u^h$ to the continuous solution $u$ using $P_2$ finite elements.
nodes.statement_short: Numerical test on $[0,1]^2$ with exact solution $u=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$, run with $P_2$ elements.

nodes.name: Coarse-grid initial guess and Newton stopping criterion
nodes.statement: On the coarse grid of size $H$, we first seek an initial guess $u_H^0$ of $u_H$ as the standard finite element approximation of the solution $u_0$ of \begin{equation*} \Delta u_0=2\sqrt{f}, \quad u_0=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*} For solving the coarse grid problem, we perform Newton's method on the coarse grid, setting the maximum iterations to 10 and we impose that the algorithm terminates when $\|u_H\|_{L^{\infty}}/ \|u^0_H\|_{L^{\infty}} \leq 10^{-6}.$
nodes.statement_short: The coarse solve is started from the FE solution of $\Delta u_0=2\sqrt f$ and Newton is capped at 10 iterations with a $10^{-6}$ relative stopping test.

nodes.name: Reported quantities and choices of the coarse-grid exponent $\lambda$
nodes.statement: We report computation times (in seconds) for the two-grid method and Newton's method on the fine grid, as well as $H^1$ errors and associated rate of convergence. See Table \ref{tab1} for $\lambda=1+ 2 \ln 2/(\ln h) =1-2/n, h=1/2^n, n=2, 3 \ldots$, and Table \ref{tab2} for $\lambda=1+ \ln 2/(\ln h)=1-1/n, h=1/2^n, n=2, 3 \ldots
nodes.statement_short: Timings, $H^1$ errors and rates are tabulated for the two choices $\lambda=1-2/n$ and $\lambda=1-1/n$.

nodes.name: Additional experiments and computational environment
nodes.statement: Experiments with $P_3$ elements gave the expected results, and so we do not report those here. We also attempted several multigrid experiments, where we interpolate between a series of meshes before ending on the fine grid. However these gave results comparable to the two-grid algorithm. At the cost of extra computation time, there is a slight increase in accuracy if a second iteration is performed on the fine grid. We do not report these results since a second iteration on the fine grid does not affect the rate of convergence of the method. The two-grid computations are accurate and fast compared with Newton's method. The computations were done in FreeFEM++ on an HP computer with Pentium dual-core 2.60 GHz processor running Windows 10.
nodes.statement_short: $P_3$ and multigrid variants gave comparable results; the two-grid method is accurate and faster than fine-grid Newton in FreeFEM++.

nodes.name: Reduce to a $W^{1,2}$ seminorm bound
nodes.statement: It is enough to prove that $|G^z_h |_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|$ which follows from the bound $| G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} $ and H\"older's inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the claim to $|G^z_h|_{W^{1,2}}\le C|\ln h|^{1/2}$ via H\"older's inequality.

nodes.name: Combine the discrete Sobolev inequality with coercivity
nodes.statement: By the discrete Sobolev inequality \cite[(4.9.2)]{Brenner08} and the coercivity of the form $A'(u; .,.)$, we have for $h$ sufficiently small \begin{align*} | A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h) | = | G^z_h (z)| \leq || G^z_h ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} || G^z_h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Conclude the logarithmic bound
nodes.statement: It follows that $$ | G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}}, $$ giving the claimed bound.
nodes.statement_short: Cancel the common factor to obtain $|G^z_h|_{W^{1,2}}\le C|\ln h|^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Expand $A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)$
nodes.statement: For $w,v \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ we have \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big(\det D^2(w+v)-\det D^2w\big)\phi\ud x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 (w+v) \}\!\} D (w+v) \] \phi \ud s - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s, \end{multline*} for all $\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write the increment of $A$ as a volume determinant difference plus two edge penalty terms.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Expand the determinant in two dimensions
nodes.statement: Since $D^2 w$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix, $\det D^2(w+v)= \det D^2 w + \det D^2 v +\cof D^2 w : D^2 v$. Thus \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\det D^2v)\phi\ud x -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\cof D^2 w: D^2v)\phi\ud x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi\ud s. + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Use $\det D^2(w+v)=\det D^2w+\det D^2v+\cof D^2w:D^2v$ to separate the linear part.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Identify the linear part $A'$ and the remainder $R$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{det2} $\cof D^2 w: D^2 v = \div\big((\cof D^2 w) D v )$. This implies that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \div \big((\cof D^2 w) D v\big) \phi \ud x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \ud s \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s, \end{align*} and $R(w;v,\phi)$ is given by \eqref{rdef1}.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\cof D^2w:D^2v$ as a divergence, giving $A'(w;v,\phi)$ and $R$ as in \eqref{rdef1}.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Integrate by parts elementwise
nodes.statement: By integration by parts and using the fact $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big((\cof D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 w) D v \] \phi \ud x \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \ud s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Move the divergence onto $D\phi$, producing an interior-edge jump term since $\phi=0$ on $\partial\Omega$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Split the jump with the product rule
nodes.statement: By \eqref{jumpaverage}, $ \[(\cof D^2 w) D v\] = \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] + \[\cof D^2 w\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\}. $ It follows that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K }\big( (\cof D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \ud x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 w)\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\} \phi \ud s \\\notag & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \ud s . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the jump-average identity so the two $\{\!\{\cof D^2w\}\!\}Dv$ terms cancel.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Specialize to $w=u$ and kill the edge terms
nodes.statement: Finally, since by assumption $u \in C^3(\Omega)$, $\[(\cof D^2 u)\]=0$. In addition, by definition $\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\}$ is continuous and $Du$ is continuous by the assumption on $u$. Thus $\[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D u \]=0$ on each interior edge. The statement about $A'(u;v,\phi)$ easily follows.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of $\cof D^2u$ and $Du$ makes both edge contributions vanish, giving \eqref{Frechet-at-u}.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Integrate the determinant identity by parts on each element
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{det1} and integration by parts \begin{multline*} \int_{K} (\det D^2 v ) \phi \ud x = \frac{1}{2} \int_{K} (\cof D^2 v ): (D^2 v) \, \phi \ud x = \frac{1}{2} \int_{K} \div\big((\cof D^2 v) D v ) \phi \ud x \\ =- \frac{1}{2} \int_K [(\cof D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \ud x + \frac{1}{2} \int_{\partial K} \big[ (\cof D^2 v) D v \big] \cdot n_K \phi \ud s. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\int_K(\det D^2v)\phi$ using $\det D^2v=\tfrac12(\cof D^2v):D^2v$ and integrate by parts.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Convert element boundary sums into edge jumps
nodes.statement: By definition of jump and since $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{\partial K} \big( (\cof D^2 v) D v \big) \cdot n_K \phi \ud s & = \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 v) D v \] \phi \ud s . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over elements so the $\partial K$ integrals become interior-edge jump integrals.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Assemble the expression for $R$
nodes.statement: We conclude that \begin{multline*} R(w;v,\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \ud x -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\cof D^2 v) D v \] \phi \ud s \\ + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\cof D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\ud s. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute back into the definition of the remainder.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Expand the jump to reach \eqref{R1-simple}
nodes.statement: Therefore, using \eqref{jumpaverage} to expand the term $\[(\cof D^2 v) D v \] $ we obtain \eqref{R1-simple}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the jump-average product rule to the term $[\![(\cof D^2v)Dv]\!]$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Decompose $A'(u;\Phi(v_h)-P_hu,\phi)$
nodes.statement: For $v_h \in B_h$, we have using \eqref{Phi-def} and \eqref{2grid-proj-def} \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) + A'(u; u - P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{split} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Insert $v_h$ and $u$ and use the definitions of $\Phi$ and of the projection $P_h$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Recognize the Taylor remainder
nodes.statement: By definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and since $A(u,\phi)=0$, we have $$ -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = A(u,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$
nodes.statement_short: Identify $-A(v_h,\phi)+A'(u;v_h-u,\phi)$ with $-R(u;v_h-u,\phi)$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Record the key identity \eqref{expr-inv}
nodes.statement: We conclude that \begin{align} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $A'(u;\Phi(v_h)-P_hu,\phi)=-R(u;v_h-u,\phi)-A'(u;I_hG-G,\phi)$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Bound the remainder term
nodes.statement: Therefore, using \eqref{R1-simple}, \eqref{w11-phi} and \eqref{Frechet-at-u}, we have \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} \\ +C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } || \phi ||_{L^1(e)} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) | \\ \leq C h^{-1} || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)|. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $R$ by the simplified formula and the edgewise $L^1$ bound, gaining a factor $h^{-1}$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Insert the $B_h$ and projection bounds
nodes.statement: By definition of $B_h$, $||v_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h |$. Moreover, by triangle inequality, \eqref{2grid-proj2} and an inverse estimate $||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq ||v_h-P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} + ||P_h u-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h | + C h^{k-1} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h | $. Thus \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C h^{k-2} |\ln h | \, || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} h^{k} |\ln h | + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| \\ \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 ) h^{k} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + | A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| . \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Use $\|v_h-u\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\le Ch^k|\ln h|$ and $\|v_h-u\|_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\le Ch^{k-1}|\ln h|$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Test with the discrete Green's functions and conclude
nodes.statement: Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain using the definition of $C_4$ $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 + C_4 ) h^{k } |\ln h|. $$ Since $C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 \leq C_4$ for $h$ sufficiently small and $k \geq 3$, we get $\|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 2 C_4 h^{k } |\ln h|$. By triangular inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ and $\phi=G^z_h$, then absorb $Ch^{k-2}|\ln h|^2\le C_4$ for small $h$, $k\ge3$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Decompose $A'(u;\Phi(v_h)-\Phi(w_h),\phi)$
nodes.statement: For $v_h$ and $w_h$ in $B_h$, we have \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- w_h,\phi) \\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad + A'(u;w_h - \Phi( w_h),\phi)\\ &= A_{}( w_h,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- w_h,\phi) \\ &= A_{}( w_h,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h -u,\phi) + A'(u; u - w_h,\phi). \end{split} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Insert $v_h$, $w_h$ and $u$ and use the definition of $\Phi$ twice.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Express the difference as a difference of remainders
nodes.statement: Since $A(u,\phi)=0$, by definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, we have $$ A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) = R(u;w_h-u,\phi) - R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $A'(u;\Phi(v_h)-\Phi(w_h),\phi)=R(u;w_h-u,\phi)-R(u;v_h-u,\phi)$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Split the remainder difference by the product identity
nodes.statement: Using algebraic manipulations of the type identified in Lemma \ref{algebraic} and \eqref{R1-simple}, we obtain \begin{multline} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 (w_h - v_h) ) D (w_h - u) ] \cdot D \phi \ud x \\ + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\cof D^2 (v_h - u) ) D (w_h - v_h) ] \cdot D \phi \ud x \\ -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \bigg( \[(\cof D^2 (w_h-v_h)) \] \{\!\{ D (w_h-u) \}\!\} + \[(\cof D^2 (v_h-u)) \] \{\!\{ D (w_h-v_h) \}\!\} \bigg) \phi \ud s \\ + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \bigg( \[ \{\!\{\cof D^2 (w_h-v_h) \}\!\} D (w_h-u) \] + \[ \{\!\{\cof D^2 (v_h-u) \}\!\} D (w_h-v_h) \] \bigg) \phi\ud s. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.4 to \eqref{R1-simple} so every term carries a factor $w_h-v_h$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Bound the split terms
nodes.statement: Arguing as in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant} and using \eqref{w11-phi}, we obtain \begin{multline*} |A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) | \leq C \Big( || w_h- v_h||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h) } ||w_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \\ + ||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \Big) ||\phi ||_{W^{1,1}}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate each product by broken $W^{2,\infty}$ times $W^{1,\infty}$ norms against $\|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}}$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Insert the $B_h$ bounds and an inverse estimate
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant}, we have $||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h|$ and recall that $||w_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h|$ by definition of $B_h$. Moreover, by an inverse estimate $|| w_h- v_h||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h) } \leq C h^{-1} || w_h- v_h||_{W^{1,\infty} }$. We conclude that $$ |A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) | \leq C\big( h^{k-1} |\ln h|+h^{k-1} |\ln h| \big)||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}||\phi ||_{W^{1,1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Use $\|v_h-u\|_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\le Ch^{k-1}|\ln h|$ and $\|w_h-v_h\|_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\le Ch^{-1}\|w_h-v_h\|_{W^{1,\infty}}$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Test with the Green's functions and conclude contraction
nodes.statement: Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h) \|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C ( h^{k-1}+h^{k-1} )|\ln h|^2 ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}, $$ that is, for $k \geq 2$ and $h$ sufficiently small, we have $ \|\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h) \|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 1/2 ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce the Lipschitz constant $Ch^{k-1}|\ln h|^2\le 1/2$ for $k\ge2$ and $h$ small.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Recall the two expressions derived in the previous proofs
nodes.statement: The proof is based on the expression \eqref{expr-con} of $A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi)$ derived in the proof of Lemma \ref{contraction} and the expression \eqref{expr-inv} of $A'(u; \Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi )$ derived in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant}.
nodes.statement_short: The argument rests on \eqref{expr-con} from the contraction proof and \eqref{expr-inv} from the invariance proof.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Split $A'(u;u_h-P_hu,\phi)$ into two pieces
nodes.statement: Since $\Phi(u_h) = u_h$, we have \begin{align} \begin{split} A'(u; u_h - P_h u,\phi) & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - P_h u,\phi) \\ & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi) + A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi). \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Use the fixed point property to write the error as a contraction term plus a consistency term.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Bound the contraction term
nodes.statement: In view of \eqref{expr-con}, we obtain \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u-u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + \\ C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h- P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \\ + C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)}. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $|A'(u;\Phi(u_h)-\Phi(P_hu),\phi)|$ by four products of broken and edge norms.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Insert the $W^{2,\infty}$ bounds
nodes.statement: By an inverse estimate, Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm}, triangle inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, we have $||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| $. Similarly, using \eqref{2grid-proj2}, we have $||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h|$.
nodes.statement_short: Both $\|u_h-P_hu\|_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)}$ and $\|u_h-u\|_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)}$ are $O(h^{k-1}|\ln h|)$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Remove the edge norms of $P_hu-u_h$
nodes.statement: Next, by the scaled trace inverse inequality \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}( K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{-1} || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Trace inverse inequality plus Cauchy-Schwarz gives an $h^{-1}$ loss only.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Estimate the edge seminorm of $P_hu-u$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{bramble}, an inverse estimate and \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} \begin{align*} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}\\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split through $I_hu$ and use the boundary gradient estimate.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Use the optimal $H^1$ projection bound
nodes.statement: We have $|| P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k ||u||_{H^{k+1}}$. This follows from \cite[Theorem 5.4.4]{Brenner08} in the case of homogeneous boundary conditions. The proof of the general case is similar to \eqref{2grid-proj1}. Thus $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ^2 \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} \leq C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Insert $\|P_hu-u\|_{H^1}\le Ch^k\|u\|_{H^{k+1}}$ to get an $O(h^{k-1/2})$ edge sum.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Bound the remaining edge sum
nodes.statement: As with \eqref{u-p-03}, by \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it follows that \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2} } \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz and the trace inverse inequality give an $O(h^{k-1})$ bound.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Collect the four contributions
nodes.statement: We conclude from \eqref{u-p-02}--\eqref{u-p-04} that \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Assemble the bounds \eqref{u-p-02}--\eqref{u-p-04} into a single estimate.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Absorb the suboptimal $W^{1,\infty}$ estimate
nodes.statement: Therefore since by Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm} we have the suboptimal estimate $ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^k | \ln h| $ \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}\\ \leq C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Insert $\|u_h-P_hu\|_{H^1}\le Ch^k|\ln h|$ to reach $Ch^k\|\phi\|_{H^1}$ for $k\ge3$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Treat the consistency term
nodes.statement: By \eqref{expr-inv}, we have $$ A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;P_h u-u,\phi) + A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). $$
nodes.statement_short: Express $A'(u;\Phi(P_hu)-P_hu,\phi)$ through the remainder at $P_hu$ and the boundary extension term.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Bound the consistency term
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{R1-simple} and inverse estimates as for \eqref{u-p-04}, we obtain \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} +C\|I_hG-G\|_{H^1}\|\phi\|_{H^1}, \end{multline*} i.e. \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ( h^{k-1} |\ln h| h^k + h^{k-2} |\ln h| h^k + h^k ) ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: The same estimates give $Ch^k\|\phi\|_{H^1}$ for $k\ge3$.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Choose the test function and conclude
nodes.statement: Taking $\phi = u_h - P_h u $ in \eqref{u-p-01} and using \eqref{u-p-05} and \eqref{u-p-06}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality and $k \geq 3$, for $h$ sufficiently small $$ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq Ch^k. $$ This completes the proof by a triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Set $\phi=u_h-P_hu$, use Poincar\'e's inequality and finish with a triangle inequality.
nodes.section: 3 $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimates for the $C^0$ Interior penalty discretization

nodes.name: Express the two-grid error through the coarse-grid remainder
nodes.statement: By definition of the two-grid algorithm, the definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for $\phi \in V_h\cap W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$, we have \begin{align*} A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi)&= A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_H-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A(u_H,\phi) \\ & = A(u_h,\phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi) = - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The algorithm's definition gives $A'(u_H;u_h-u^h,\phi)=-R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)$.

nodes.name: Shift the bilinear form from $u_H$ to $u$
nodes.statement: It follows that \begin{align*} A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi)& = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Add and subtract $A'(u-u_H;u_h-u^h,\phi)$.

nodes.name: Bound the shifted form
nodes.statement: With arguments similar to the ones used in the proof of Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm}, we have \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the estimates of the previous proof to control $|A'(u;u_h-u^h,\phi)|$.

nodes.name: Estimate the coarse edge seminorm of $u-u_H$
nodes.statement: But, using \eqref{bramble}, \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} and an inverse estimate \begin{align*} | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | u - I_H u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}( K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}( K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} ( K)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split through $I_Hu$ and use the boundary gradient estimate on the coarse mesh.

nodes.name: Aggregate over elements
nodes.statement: It follows that $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} }. $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum the elementwise bounds into an $\ell^2$ edge estimate.

nodes.name: Insert the coarse-grid $H^1$ estimate
nodes.statement: We therefore obtain from \eqref{nodal-interpolant} and Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3.7 on the coarse mesh reduces the bound to $CH^{k-1/2}\|u\|_{H^{k+1}}$.

nodes.name: Bound the mixed edge sum
nodes.statement: By Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, \eqref{trace-inverse} and an inverse estimate, it follows that $$ \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{- \frac{3}{2}} H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Obtain an $O(h^{-3/2}H^{k-1/2})$ factor multiplying $\|u_h-u^h\|_{H^1}$.

nodes.name: Assemble the estimate \eqref{u-p-07}
nodes.statement: Therefore, since $|| u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C H^{k-1} |\ln H|$ and by the discrete Sobolev inequality, c.f. \cite{Bramble86}, $|| \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C (1+ | \ln h|^{ 1/2 }) ||\phi||_{H^1}$, we obtain from \eqref{u-p-066} \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} | \ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1} + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \\ \leq C h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the pieces using the discrete Sobolev inequality for $\|\phi\|_{L^\infty}$.

nodes.name: Bound the coarse-grid remainder
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{R1-simple} and the trace estimates \eqref{trace-inverse} and \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{multline} |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \leq C || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^{-2} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $|R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|$ by $Ch^{-2}\|u_h-u_H\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\|u_h-u_H\|_{H^1}\|\phi\|_{H^1}$.

nodes.name: Choose the test function
nodes.statement: Taking $\phi = u_h - u^h $ in \eqref{u-p-07} and using \eqref{u-p-08}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality, Theorems \ref{2grid-imp-thm} and \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} for $k \geq 3$ and $h$ sufficiently small \begin{multline*} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C (h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| + H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| ) || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \\ +C h^{-2} (h^{k} |\ln h | + H^{k} |\ln H |) (h^k+H^k). \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Set $\phi=u_h-u^h$ and use Poincar\'e's inequality together with Theorems 3.6 and 3.7.

nodes.name: Choose the exponent $\lambda$
nodes.statement: We conclude that for $H=h^{\lambda}$, $\lambda > \max \{1/(k-1), 3/(2k-1) \} = 3/(2k-1)$ and $k \geq 3$, $$ || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{-2} |\ln H \, | H^{2k}. $$ We therefore get $||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k$ provided $\lambda > 3/(2k-1)$ and $2 \lambda k -2- \epsilon > k$ for some $\epsilon \in (0,1) $, that is $\lambda > \max \{ (k+2+ \epsilon)/(2k), 3/(2k-1) \} = 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Absorb the left-hand factor for $\lambda>3/(2k-1)$ and require $2\lambda k-2-\epsilon>k$ to reach the $O(h^k)$ rate.
